mapa.rotulo: Heat map of accidents in Porto Alegre

ressalva: The data shows incidents recorded by EPTC, the city traffic agency. A hot spot on the map means a concentration of records, not driver blame or the cause of the accidents.

metodologia.fonteTexto: Open dataset “Acidentes de Trânsito – Acidentes” (traffic accidents), published by the City of Porto Alegre on the #DataPoa portal, with records from EPTC.
metodologia.extracao: Dataset extracted on {{data}}. Loaded into the system on {{carga}}.
metodologia.periodoTexto: The dataset covers {{inicio}} to {{fim}}. The dashboard opens with the last 5 calendar years of data, from {{padraoInicio}} to {{padraoFim}}.
metodologia.criterioTexto: A place is critical when it has {{n}} or more accidents within {{raio}} m. The calculation starts from the accident with the most neighbours within the radius, forms the spot and removes those accidents from the pool. It repeats until no group of {{n}} or more remains, so each accident counts in a single spot.
metodologia.criterioN: The value {{n}} came from the exploratory analysis of the dataset: it is the level that separates intersections with persistent concentration from the rest of the city.
metodologia.viasTexto: The dataset has no road type field. The classification uses the prefix the City writes before each street name: AV (avenue), R (street), ESTR (road). Other prefixes, such as lane, square and tunnel, go into “Other”.
metodologia.horarioTexto: Filters combine with each other. A record with no time in the dataset shows normally, but leaves the selection when a time filter is on. The day of the week is calculated from the date.
metodologia.descartesTexto: Of {{lidos}} records read, {{descartados}} were left off the map ({{percentual}}).
metodologia.ressalvaVolume: The map does not account for traffic volume. Busy roads tend to have more records.
